newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan-Kuwait sees capital raise approval.
newsitem.headline: Jordan-Kuwait sees capital raise approval.

text.p: Jordan Kuwait Bank said on Monday it expected approval for plans to double its capital to 20 million dinars ($28 million) despite opposition from dissenting shareholders.

Opponents of the plan withdrew from Sunday's extraordinary general assembly, held to discuss the capital increase, denying it a quorum. They said papers nominating representatives of some Gulf Arab shareholders, who support the capital rise, were incorrectly submitted.
"When they noticed we had a majority they left, so the meeting could not reach its quorum," bank chairman Sufian al-Sartawi said. "We needed 50 percent and we had 48 percent."
But he told Reuters he was confident the rescheduled assembly on July 15 would attract enough shareholders, with or without dissenters, to approve the plan.
Shareholders opposing the capital increase are led by Tawfiq Fakhouri, chairman of Bank of Jordan, which has promoted a merger between the two banks.

The Central Bank has been trying to strengthen Jordan's banking system by encouraging mergers between smaller banks and setting all banks a minimum capital level of 20 million dinars by the end of 1997.
Sartawi has said the majority of shareholders supported the capital increase rather than a merger, especially after recent bloc purchases of shares by Kuwaiti and Gulf Arab investors.
If the capital raise is approved next week by shareholders the bank will move 4.5 million dinars from reserves and retained profits and raise another 5.5 million through share subscription.
